note_on_gaps: All eight required axes now have at least one verified rights-clear source. Two caveats carry forward honestly: (1) no source in this set is a true multi-host studio podcast recorded as such — royal-society-cloke is a two-host conversational interview, which is the closest rights-clear fit found; (2) hadhazy-protest's audio difficulty is inferred from its recording context, not measured. C-SPAN and NASA press briefings were investigated and rejected: C-SPAN items on archive.org carry licenseurl=null (rights unconfirmed), and NASA press conferences at ~634 MB exceed the host's storage headroom.
findings_before_corpus_ran: telugu-launch: the raw .ogv is structurally damaged (non-monotonic DTS, mis-marked keyframes). Transcribing it directly produced 0 segments and the pipeline diagnosed 'no audible spoken content' — a misdiagnosis, since a clean remux of the same file transcribes to 11 segments. The pipeline's no-speech error therefore conflates two unrelated causes: genuinely speechless media and an unreadable container. This is the single most misleading failure mode in the product, because it tells a user their source has no speech when it has plenty.

ooi-vertical: AV1/Opus WebM. Input seeking past ~15 s dropped the audio stream from the rendered deliverable on 7 of 8 sampled positions, while the container provably holds 7601 audio packets across all 152 s. ffmpeg reported no error. The deliverable would have shipped silent; engine/qa.py caught it and failed the run. Fixed in engine/render.py by probing each part for audio and falling back to output seeking.
